title: ERC-8004: Trustless Agents
quote: This protocol proposes to use blockchains to discover, choose, and interact with agents across organizational boundaries without pre-existing trust, thus enabling open-ended agent economies.

title: ERC-8004 Spec (Jan 2026 Update) — Validation Registry section
quote: function validationRequest(address validatorAddress, uint256 agentId, string requestURI, bytes32 requestHash) external — This function MUST be called by the owner or operator of agentId. The requestURI points to off-chain data containing all information needed for the validator to validate, including inputs and outputs needed for the verification. The requestHash is a commitment to this data (keccak256 of the request payload). function validationResponse(bytes32 requestHash, uint8 response, string responseURI, bytes32 responseHash, string tag) external — Only requestHash and response are mandatory. The response is a value between 0 and 100. validationResponse() can be called multiple times for the same requestHash, enabling use cases like progressive validation states. Incentives and slashing related to validation are managed by the specific validation protocol and are outside the scope of this registry.

title: ValidationRegistry.sol — Reference Implementation (Jan 2026 Update)
quote: require(validatorAddress != agentOwner, "Self-validation not allowed"); require(!_requestExists[requestHash], "Request hash already exists"); ... Only the designated validator may call validationResponse; response is checked require(response <= 100). The contract stores Request and Response structs and exposes getValidationStatus, getSummary, getAgentValidations, getValidatorRequests. WARNING: This section is still under active updates with the TEE community. Expect further changes later in 2026. Consider this EXPERIMENTAL.

title: erc-8004/erc-8004-contracts — canonical CC0 registry contracts (Identity/Reputation/Validation, Upgradeable)
quote: Repository implements ERC-8004 (Trustless Agents): upgradeable IdentityRegistry, ReputationRegistry, and ValidationRegistry contracts under CC0-1.0. Top-level Solidity files include ValidationRegistryUpgradeable.sol alongside ERC8004SPEC.md. Tested with Hardhat. The Validation Registry portion of the ERC-8004 spec is still under active update and discussion with the TEE community.

title: ERC-8004: Trustless Agents — discussions
quote: spengrah: 'I don't see a way in the current standard for an arbitrary smart contract to read the result of a validation response.' Marco-MetaMask: keeping ratings and validation responses off-chain was deliberate, since single entries require aggregation anyway, and for gas efficiency. spengrah proposes minimal additions such as a getValidationResponse() function enabling contract queries and optional on-chain feedback records.

title: Phala-Network/erc-8004-tee-agent — ERC-8004 Compliant TEE Agent with TEE Registry Extension
quote: TEERegistry maps agentId to TEE keys, each carrying (teeArch, codeMeasurement, pubkey, codeConfigUri, verifier). addKey is gated by a whitelisted verifier that should validate (1) the TEE attestation, (2) that codeMeasurement matches the public input in the proof, (3) that pubkey matches the public input in the proof — a CVM-on-Phala Cloud pattern that plugs the TEE attestation evidence under the ERC-8004 Validation flow.

title: Trustless Agents — with zkML (JOLT-Atlas)
quote: Agent executes ML inference, JOLT-Atlas generates a ZK proof of execution, dataHash commits to the proof and verification parameters, the validator contract verifies the proof on-chain, the ValidationResponse records the verification result, and the reputation system updates based on cryptographic validation. Practical for small models today; large LLMs still take minutes.

title: ERC-8004: a practical explainer for trustless agents
quote: The Validation Registry standardises hooks for stake-secured re-execution, zkML and TEE oracles. Economics — collateral, rewards, penalties — are not specified by the registry; security depends on the validator chosen.

title: ERC-8004: Infrastructure for Autonomous AI Agents
quote: ERC-8004 does not specify economic incentives for validators; security depends on composing higher-level protocols. Capability verification is not provided by registration alone — trust signals depend on validators that may themselves need to be trusted or staked.

title: ERC-8004 Explained: Ethereum's AI Agent Standard Guide 2025
quote: The Identity Registry provides portable agent identifiers using ERC-721; the Reputation Registry enables standardized feedback and rating collection; and the Validation Registry supports cryptographic and economic verification of agent work.

title: Ethereum's ERC-8004 aims to put identity and trust behind AI agents
quote: ERC-8004 gives AI agents a verifiable on-chain identity, a reputation system, and a mechanism for independent task validation; co-authored by contributors from MetaMask, the Ethereum Foundation, Google, and Coinbase.

title: ERC-8004 Mainnet Launch: What This Agent Protocol Actually Does
quote: Within the first month of mainnet, more than 45,000 AI agents had registered across multiple blockchains according to 8004 Scan. The standard has received backing from ENS, EigenLayer, The Graph, and Taiko.

title: BNB Chain Backs ERC-8004 for On-chain AI Identities
quote: BNB Chain deployed ERC-8004 on both BSC mainnet and testnet, positioning itself as 'an early hub for agent systems that require low fees and fast execution.' Over 24,000 agent identities tracked on Ethereum-based deployments at time of writing.
